strategy.summary: GET /products (src/app.js listProducts) filters the in-memory catalogue by a case-insensitive name substring `q`, pages it with `limit` (default 20, capped at MAX_LIMIT=50) and `offset` (default 0), returns { total, items }, and rejects non-whole limit/offset or limit < 1 with 400. The tests start the real app on an OS-chosen port, as test/products.test.js does, and prove each rule through HTTP.
inScope: GET /products: q filtering, listing without q, limit/offset paging, total, limit cap, 400 validation
outOfScope: GET /products/:id and POST /orders (not part of this ticket)
Updating the README's stale 'up to 100' (reviewer said to leave it)
assumptions: The cap is 50, as in the code (MAX_LIMIT); the reviewer confirmed this in Q1. The README's 'up to 100' is out of date and stays as it is.
The tests import DEFAULT_LIMIT and MAX_LIMIT from src/app.js rather than writing the numbers out.
The catalogue is the fixed 120-product list in src/catalogue.js (15 of each of 8 names, ids in order), so expected totals and ids are known. GET requests don't change it.
No services are faked: the real app runs in-process on port 0, as the existing test does.

risks.description: Case-insensitive matching could break for mixed-case queries
risks.mitigation: TC1 uses a mixed-case q and checks the exact total and names

risks.description: Cap bypass lets clients request the whole catalogue
risks.mitigation: TC6 asks for more than the cap and asserts exactly MAX_LIMIT items

risks.description: Loose number parsing accepts decimals or negatives
risks.mitigation: TC8–TC10 check 400 for each invalid form

acceptanceCriteria.text: q matches products whose name contains it, in any case; without q every product is listed.
Results are paged by limit and offset, the response gives the total number of matches, and limits above the cap (50) are capped.
A limit or offset that isn't a whole number, or a limit below 1, is refused with 400.

review.standard: Reuse the repo's helpers ... A helper two specs need goes once in their shared base or a helper module
review.summary: The in-process server start/stop (beforeAll listen(0) / afterAll close and the `base` URL) is copied line for line from test/products.test.js lines 4-13 rather than moved into a shared test helper both files import.
review.failureScenario: If server startup changes (e.g. createApp gains an option, or the close needs a timeout so a hung keep-alive connection doesn't stall teardown), only one of test/products.test.js and test/products-search.test.js gets the fix, and the other keeps the old setup. What the tests prove doesn't change today. A small test/support/server.js exporting a startServer()/stop pair that both files use would remove the copy.

review.standard: Vitest: Parametrisation - use it.each when the behaviour is identical and only the data varies
review.summary: TC8 and TC10 loop over the invalid values inside one `it` instead of using `it.each`, so the first failing value stops the others from running and the report shows only one test per parameter.
review.failureScenario: If the app wrongly accepted limit=abc, the loop at line 81 (and the same pattern at line 93 for offset) would stop at 'abc', and the results for '2.5' and '-3' would never be reported, so you can't tell whether one rule broke or all three. Each row still has a labelled assertion, so the test can't pass wrongly. `it.each(['abc','2.5','-3'])('refuses limit=%s with 400', ...)` would report each value on its own.

questions.question: The README says GET /products `limit` goes "up to 100", but the code caps it at 50 (MAX_LIMIT in src/app.js). Which cap is right?
questions.assumption: I'll test what the code does: a page holds at most MAX_LIMIT items, using the constant imported from src/app.js, so the test follows the code. I'll note the README mismatch as an open question.
questions.answer: The cap is 50, as the code does. The README is out of date; leave it as it is and test against 50.
